headline: Recommitted a proposed public camping ordinance to the City Manager and adopted a GreenTech Park tax increment financing zone and Lakeside Avenue housing tax agreement.
summary: The council recommitted a proposed public camping ordinance to the City Manager by an 8-1 vote. It adopted orders on shelter funding and winter shelter planning, and orders asking for a contractor list and a wage report related to Optiline Enterprises, a subcontractor on the 274 Franklin St. project. It also referred many street, sidewalk, and traffic petitions to committees.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 8, 2026 City Council meeting.
Approved National Grid conduit permission for Gates St. after a hearing with no speakers.
Approved National Grid conduit permission for Patch St.
Referred the Winter Heights granite survey marker petition to Public Works Committee.
Referred the request to give Laurel St. the honorary name Arries Ann Ward Way to Public Works Committee.
Placed on file the request for multiple speed humps on Harrington Way.
Referred the Montague St. speed hump petition and related traffic petitions (items 8d through 8f, 8h, 8j through 8q, and 8s) to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Placed on file the request for a stop sign on Charlton St. at Beacon St.
Referred the Holden St. truck ban petition, as amended, to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Referred the Southbridge St. and Hammond St. signal review request, as amended, to Traffic and Parking Committee.
Referred the Institute Pond wildlife petition to Veterans' Memorials, Parks and Recreation Committee.
Adopted items 9a through 9o, except 9c, 9d and 9g, by a 10-0 roll call vote with Toomey recused. Item 9l was adopted as amended.
Held under privilege by Councilor King the request for a draft ordinance increasing noise fines (item 9c).
Held under privilege by Councilor King the review of public hearings for one-day event licenses (item 9d) and the staffing report request (item 9g).
Adopted as amended the request for a discussion of a new Rule 61 on annual department reports, by a 10-1 vote (Blotta opposed).
Adopted as amended the request for a discussion of a new Rule 62 on budget recommendations, by an 8-3 vote (Blotta, King and Ojeda opposed).
Adopted as amended the request for a discussion of a new Rule 63 on a preliminary budget, by a 10-1 vote (Blotta opposed).
Placed on file the request for increased traffic enforcement on Harrington Way.
Adopted the request that the Commissioner of Health and Human Services work with Worcester Community Midwifery.
Adopted, by an 11-0 vote, the request for a report on adding a recycling bin at the Clark St. Drop-Off Site.
Adopted, by a 10-0 vote with Toomey recused, the request for draft rules to license and register motorized scooters and bikes.
Held under privilege the requests on a New Homeowner and Tenant Summit (10h), a mitigation and community benefits policy (10i), and permanent public bathrooms (10j).
Referred the request for a joint meeting with the Board of Health to Public Health and Human Services Committee, by an 11-0 vote.
Held under privilege by Councilor Rosen the request on Optiline Enterprises work at the 274 Franklin St. project.

Held under privilege by Councilor Petty the requests on Oriental St. potholes, Bay State Rd. manhole, 2 Intervale Rd. sidewalk, Columbus Park area safety, Worcester State and May Street enforcement, and Doherty Memorial High School lot (items 10m through 10r).
Held under privilege by Councilor Petty the requests for Homeless Strategic Plan reports and updates on earlier homeless-related orders (items 10s through 10y).
Held under privilege by Councilor Bilotta the request to use opioid settlement funds for public bathroom monitoring staff (item 10z).
Referred items 12a through 12d on the City Charter and related communications to Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, by an 11-0 vote.
Referred the 25 West Chester St. Adaptive Re-use Overlay District zoning petition to Economic Development Committee, by an 8-1 vote (Economou opposed; King and Rivera abstained).
Referred the 128 Providence St. and 95 Vernon St. zoning map petitions to Economic Development Committee, by an 11-0 vote.
Adopted the resolution establishing a Tax Increment Financing Zone for GreenTech Park, by an 11-0 vote.
Adopted the resolution approving an Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing Agreement for 16-32 Lakeside Avenue and 18-20 Garland Avenue, by an 11-0 vote.
Accepted financial and OPEB reports (items 15a through 15h) by an 11-0 vote, with each recommended to be placed on file.
Accepted the committee report on the noise ordinance order, by a 10-0 vote with Toomey recused, which recommended the order be placed on file.
Accepted the report on the Hospital Guard of the Worcester Police Department, by a 10-0 vote with Toomey absent.
Adopted the orders on items 17a through 17h, including sidewalk, guardrail, bollard, sewer, streetlight, and signage requests, by an 11-0 vote.
Accepted items 17i through 17o by an 11-0 vote. Two petitions were placed on file, and five streetlight petitions were granted leave to withdraw.
Referred the Tom Marino police reform petition to Public Safety Committee.
Denied Councilor King's motion to place the Public Camping Ordinance item on file, by a 1-9 vote.
Recommitted the proposed Public Camping Ordinance and the Disrupting the Cycle framework to the City Manager, by an 8-1 vote (Bergman opposed; King abstained).

Adopted nine orders from the Public Camping Ordinance item covering shelter funding, bathroom best practices, a winter overflow shelter, displacement, state advocacy, a winter shelter readiness report, encampment maps, clinical co-responses, and a stakeholder meeting.
Adopted the order asking the City Manager to provide developers with a list of contractors ineligible under the Responsible Development Ordinance, by an 11-0 vote.
Adopted the order asking the City Manager for a report on wage theft issues related to Optiline Enterprises, by an 11-0 vote.
Denied the rules suspension to allow an executive session, by a 6-5 vote. Eight votes were required.
Adopted the order asking for a report on best practices for street and sidewalk rehabilitation timelines, by an 11-0 vote.
Adopted the suspension of Rule 21 to let Councilor Fresolo speak beyond ten minutes on item #8.11A CM, by an 11-0 vote.
Adopted the order asking for a detailed process for selecting streets and sidewalks for rehabilitation, by an 11-0 vote.
Adopted the order asking for a report on how the dissolution of CMRPHA affected support for the unhoused population, by an 11-0 vote.
Referred the order on social service agencies working with homeless and addiction programs to Public Health and Human Services Committee, by a 10-0 vote.
Adopted the suspension of rules to let Councilor Fresolo discuss a matter not on the agenda, by an 11-0 vote.
Denied the order to meet in executive session on police officer conduct, by a 4-6 vote.
Adopted the order asking the Mayor for a report on Rules 48 and 49 and charter language on appointments, by a 10-0 vote.
